claims.text: The driver's own cancellation reason code is DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which POL-NS-01(d) names as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. Limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT; DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is none of those, so limb (d) fails and the fee is not chargeable under the anchor clause.

The driver's in-geofence dwell was 380 seconds, which is short of the 300 second minimum dwell for a STANDARD zone class. The shortfall is 200 seconds against the required minimum, so even on the driver's best case the waiting period was not served and the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-06.

The rider was present and coordinating: her GPS track places her device within 15.5 m of the pickup pin for the whole window (67 qualifying fixes, all inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius), and she answered the driver's message at 12:00:59 saying she was at the lift lobby. The driver never replied and never placed an in-app call before cancelling at 12:06:23, so POL-NS-04 exonerates the rider and the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

The rider's own profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, so neither the POL-NS-09(d) abuse trigger nor the POL-NS-09(c) repeat-dispute trigger is engaged on the rider's side. There is no basis to treat this as a rider-abuse case.

The fare breakdown shows the full SGD 4.50 cancellation fee was charged to the rider and no refund has been issued (refund_issued_sgd 0.0, payment_status CHARGED). The contested amount is therefore live and a full refund of the cancellation-fee line is the correct remedy.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run: there is no advisory covering the pickup road and no basis to accumulate separate in-geofence intervals. The driver cannot rely on limb (i) to extend his dwell, and the 380 second run stands as the measured dwell.

claims.text: The driver's own trace places him inside the STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous 380-second run, from 11:59:59 to 12:06:19, which is well past the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip. The dwell is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, exactly as POL-NS-01(c) requires, and the run is unbroken: 39 qualifying fixes, no gaps, 100% coverage.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 11:59:59, and the GPS trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at the same second, so the arrival marker is corroborated rather than false. There is no clock skew between the two artifacts and no motion at the marker: the driver's distinct speeds include 0.0 kph and the arrival run is stationary. POL-NS-05 therefore does not displace the waiting clock, and the dwell stands at 380 seconds.

The rider's own device was inside the 100 m rider-presence radius for the whole window: 67 qualifying fixes, all of them qualifying, mean distance 11.7 m from the pin, max 15.5 m, and a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph. The rider was stationary at the pickup point and did not board. That is the factual core of a no-show, and it is recorded on the rider's own track, not merely inferred from the driver's.

The chat log shows the driver asked 'cannot find you, where are you' at 12:00:29 and the rider answered 'at the lift lobby' at 12:00:59. The rider's answer names a sub-location but the driver had already been holding position inside the geofence for 30 seconds and continued to hold it for a further 5 minutes 20 seconds after that message before cancelling at 12:06:23. The driver did not abandon the pickup; he waited out the full free period and beyond.

The cancellation was recorded by the driver under reason code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE. I concede that this code is not one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, and that on the face of the clause limb (d) therefore fails. I do not stretch the record to call it RIDER_NO_SHOW. The consequence is that the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01, and the refund route must be found elsewhere in the category.

The driver's stationary fixes are inside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius, not outside it, so POL-NS-03 does not apply and the wrong-entrance route is closed. The rider's 'at the lift lobby' message does not identify a block, tower or bay that the driver failed to move to; it is a sub-location the driver could not act on because the rider never said which lift lobby of a Jurong West HDB block. POL-NS-03's fault allocation therefore does not strip the driver of compensation on these facts.

The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, and the driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 0 against 114 completed trips in 30 days. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires BOTH a count of 4 or more and a rate above 0.08; neither limb is met, so compensation is not withheld on that ground. I cite only the two fields POL-NS-07 and POL-NS-09(c) name, not the lifetime counters.

The fare ledger shows the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 charged to the rider, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the driver compensation computed at SGD 3.60, being 80 percent of the net fee under POL-NS-07. The fee line reconciles with the platform_policy figure of SGD 4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect and the money block is clean.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING: no advisory covers Blk 640 Jurong West St 61 in this window. I cite the absence itself. It means POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run to accumulate dwell across intervals, but it also means nothing in the record shows the driver was prevented from holding position, and the driver in fact held position for 380 seconds without needing any accumulation. The missing advisory is neutral to the driver's case and does not impair the arrival or dwell findings, which rest on the GPS trace alone.

The rider filed this dispute and the charge still stands: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves that charge in place, so declining to refund is a driver-side outcome on this record, and the driver's payout under POL-NS-07 is the affirmative remedy the case produces.

ruling.explanation: Rider and driver: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee is refunded in full. The fee charged was SGD 4.50 (EV-FARE-02723: cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Under POL-NS-01 a no-show fee is chargeable only if all four limbs hold. Limb (d) fails: the trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE (EV-TRIP-02723), which is not one of the three codes the limb recognises and which the clause treats as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. Because the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (EV-GPS-02723: one in-geofence run, 380 s, 39 qualifying fixes), POL-NS-01 directs a full refund of the cancellation fee with no driver compensation, plus the driver-education referral above. Independently, POL-NS-04 exonerates the rider: she sent a locating message during the waiting window ('at the lift lobby', 12:00:59, EV-CHAT-02723); the driver neither replied within 120 s nor made an in-app call before cancelling at 12:06:23 (EV-TRIP-02723, in_app_calls empty); and her device sat inside the 100 m rider-presence radius for all 67 of her qualifying fixes (mean 11.7 m, max 15.5 m). The refund is FULL_REFUND of the SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line. Surviving claims, answered together where they make the same point: (1) The driver's dwell point is right on the facts — the in-geofence dwell was 380 s against the 180 s free waiting period in force — and the arrival marker was not false (first in-geofence fix 11:59:59 matches the 'arrived' event, no motion at the marker), so POL-NS-05 does not move the clock. But a sufficient dwell and a true marker cannot rescue a fee whose limb (d) fails. (2) The rider's POL-NS-06 shortfall argument is rejected: 380 s exceeds the 180 s free waiting period POL-NS-01(c) requires, and the 300 s figure in fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec is a version-1 interpretive field that the resolution rule says is never applied to a record carrying platform_policy — and 380 s exceeds it in any event. (3) The driver's POL-NS-03 point is accepted: the stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, so the wrong-entrance route is closed. (4) Driver compensation of SGD 3.60 (80 percent of 4.50, EV-FARE-02723) is not payable: POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 satisfied in full, and it is not; and NO_ACTION — leaving the charge in place — is not open where limb (d) fails. (5) The anti-farming check is not tripped (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d 0 against 114 completed trips in 30 days; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d 0), and neither POL-NS-09(c) nor (d) is engaged, so there is no abuse escalation. (6) EV-ADVIS-02723-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT); it decides nothing here, because with a single in-geofence interval and a 380 s dwell there is no shortfall for POL-NS-06(i) to cure, and under POL-NS-11/NS-08 it does not impair the driver's trace or cap confidence. No artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d): no clock skew (arrival event 11:59:59 = first fix 11:59:59), no trace gap (100% coverage, 75 fixes, max gap 0 s), the chat carries the 2 messages the trip record counts, and the fare line reconciles to platform_policy at SGD 4.50 — so no escalation under POL-NS-09. Confidence is 0.95: the deciding facts rest on artifacts at weight 1.0. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, at or below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so the refund executes automatically.
referrals: POL-NS-01: driver-education item — the cancellation was recorded under reason code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three recognised no-show codes (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT); the mis-selected reason code is referred for driver education.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02723 is refunded to you in full. To the driver: the fee does not stand, and no compensation is payable to you.

The money. POL-NS-01 makes a no-show fee chargeable only if all four of its conditions hold at once. The first three do hold. The trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 11:59:59 (EV-TRIP-02723); the GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that same second, with 39 qualifying fixes and no gaps (EV-GPS-02723); and he held position for a continuous 380-second dwell against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, and 380 s is confirmed by the trace's own shortfall figure of -200 s). The fourth condition fails. The driver terminated the trip under reason code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE (EV-TRIP-02723), and POL-NS-01(d) names that code as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider — it is none of the three rider-fault codes (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). Because the driver's stationary fixes lie INSIDE the arrival radius, POL-NS-01 fixes the outcome itself: the fee is not chargeable, the ruling is FULL_REFUND of the cancellation fee with no driver compensation, and the mis-selected reason code goes into the referrals as a driver-education item.

Independently, POL-NS-04 exonerates the rider and produces the same result. She sent a locating message ('at the lift lobby') at 12:00:59 (EV-CHAT-02723); the driver did not reply within 120 seconds of it and placed no in-app call before cancelling at 12:06:23 (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty); and her own track places her device within 15.5 m of the pin for all 67 qualifying fixes, well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius (EV-GPS-02723).

The driver's claims. The 380-second in-geofence dwell, the corroborated arrival marker and the rider's stationary track are all accepted — the arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05, because at 11:59:59 the driver was inside the geofence and stationary, not more than 300 m out or moving at 15 km/h. But they do not save the fee, because limb (d) fails and POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full. Your request for SGD 3.60 compensation under POL-NS-07 is therefore refused: that clause pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full or POL-NS-10(g) applies, and neither is so. The anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against 114 completed trips in 30 days, and both the count and the rate must be met), but passing that check gates a payout the clause never reaches. POL-NS-03 does not apply either: it governs only where the driver's stationary fixes are OUTSIDE the arrival radius, and here they are inside it. Your argument that NO_ACTION would be a driver-side outcome is correct as far as it goes, but the record does not produce NO_ACTION — the driver's own reason code bars the charge.

The rider's claims. Your limb-(d) point under POL-NS-01 is accepted and is the ground of the ruling. Your POL-NS-06 claim asserting a 300-second minimum dwell, with a 200-second shortfall, is rejected: 300 seconds is the legacy fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec figure, which the fee schedule's own resolution rule says is never applied to a record that carries platform_policy; the period in force here is the 180-second free wait, and the 380-second dwell exceeds it. Your conclusion is right, but that route does not carry it. Your point that the traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02723-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) leaves POL-NS-06(i) unavailable is accepted, and it changes nothing because no interval accumulation is needed on these facts.

Confidence and execution. Every artifact that carries a deciding fact — the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare ledger — has weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; the missing advisory carries no deciding fact and does not lower it. Confidence is 0.95. No POL-NS-08 impairment applies (no clock skew, no gap above 120 s, no missing chat message, and the SGD 4.50 fee line reconciles with the platform figure). The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so the refund executes on issue. The fee line is drawn from fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee = SGD 4.50 (total_charged SGD 4.50, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).
referrals: POL-NS-01 — driver-education item: the trip was terminated under reason code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which does not support a no-show fee. The driver should be reminded to record RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT where the rider genuinely failed to appear.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged to the rider is refunded in full (amount_sgd 4.50), and no driver compensation is payable (driver_compensation_sgd null). This is a provisional ruling made without human review. Either party may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04, and the monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so the refund executes automatically.

What happened is not seriously disputed. DRV-09723 was assigned at 11:54:58, tapped 'I'm Here' at 11:59:59, and the GPS trace EV-GPS-02723 places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 11:59:59 to 12:06:19 — a continuous 380-second in-geofence run of 39 qualifying fixes, no gaps, 100% coverage. The rider's own track in the same trace sits within 15.5 m of the pin for the whole window. In chat (EV-CHAT-02723) the driver asked 'cannot find you, where are you' at 12:00:29 and the rider answered 'at the lift lobby' at 12:00:59.

Two independent routes make the fee unchargeable.

First, POL-NS-01 limb (d). The anchor clause requires the trip to be terminated under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. The trip record EV-TRIP-02723 shows cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which POL-NS-01(d) itself names as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider and which does not satisfy limb (d). The driver's advocate conceded exactly this, and the driver's own counterparty statement says the same. POL-NS-01's own text then fixes the outcome for this configuration: where the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, the fee is not chargeable, the ruling is FULL_REFUND of the cancellation fee with no driver compensation, and the mis-selected reason code is referred as a driver-education item. That is this case — the fixes are inside the radius, not outside it, so POL-NS-03 does not apply.

Second, POL-NS-04. (a) The rider sent a locating message inside the waiting window ('at the lift lobby' — an entrance identifier). (b) The driver neither replied in chat within 120 seconds of that message nor placed an in-app call before cancelling (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty). (c) The rider's own track puts her within the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius on every qualifying fix. All three limbs hold, so the rider is exonerated and the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

The driver's surviving arguments are answered. The 380-second dwell does exceed the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, the figure read from the record itself), and the arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05 — the 11:59:59 marker matches the first qualifying in-geofence fix and the driver was stationary at it — but neither fact makes the fee chargeable, because limb (d) is the rider-fault limb and the driver's own reason code defeats it. EV-FARE-02723 shows the fee line of SGD 4.50 reconciles with platform_policy, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect, but that only confirms the amount, not its chargeability; the computed driver compensation of SGD 3.60 is not payable because POL-NS-07 pays only on a fee that survives POL-NS-01. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d 0 against 114 completed trips in 30 days), so compensation is not withheld on that ground — it simply never arises. The NO_ACTION argument is rejected: POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative on a rider-filed dispute, and it cannot be used to convert a failed limb (d) into a driver payout.

The rider's advocate's POL-NS-06 submission is rejected on the merits: the required minimum dwell for this record is the 180-second free waiting period the record carries, not the 300-second version-1 figure, which fee_schedule says is never applied to a record carrying platform_policy; 380 seconds exceeds 180 seconds, so there is no shortfall and no refund route is needed under POL-NS-06.

No escalation applies. Confidence is above the POL-NS-09 floor of 0.70; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; neither party's repeat-dispute counters reach POL-NS-09(c) or (d); and no deciding fact rests on an impaired artifact. The only artifact below full weight is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02723-01, which is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); nobody needs it, because the driver held one continuous 380-second run and never required accumulated dwell, so it carries no deciding fact and does not cap confidence under POL-GEN-02(2). All artifacts that do carry the deciding facts (EV-TRIP-02723, EV-GPS-02723, EV-CHAT-02723) stand at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0.

One submission was discarded at the citation check: the driver's claim resting on the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02723-01 failed to disclose that artifact's impairment and issue code, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires.

ruling.explanation: Rider and driver: this dispute turns on the driver's own trace and trip record, and both are clean. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 11:59:59 and the GPS trace's first in-geofence fix is at the same second, so the arrival marker is true, not false; the trace puts the driver at the pin (minimum distance 0 m), stationary, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for an unbroken 380-second run (39 qualifying fixes, 11:59:59-12:06:19, 100% coverage, no gaps), against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force in trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec. The rider's own track places her device 8.4-15.5 m from the pin throughout (67 qualifying fixes), and the chat log shows the driver asking 'cannot find you, where are you' at 12:00:29 and the rider answering 'at the lift lobby' at 12:00:59, with no driver reply and no in-app call before the cancellation at 12:06:23. The charge does not stand. The driver terminated the trip under cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, and POL-NS-01(d) recognises only RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT; the clause states expressly that DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider and does not satisfy limb (d). Because the stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius rather than outside it, POL-NS-01's mis-selected-code branch applies: the fee is not chargeable, the outcome is FULL_REFUND of the cancellation fee with no driver compensation, and the mis-selected code is referred for driver education. Independently, POL-NS-04 exonerates the rider: she sent a locating message inside the waiting window, the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app call, and her device was inside the 100 m rider-presence radius on every qualifying fix - so the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation. POL-NS-06 does not apply: the effective dwell of 380 seconds exceeds the 180-second free waiting period (the derived shortfall field is -200 s, i.e. a 200-second surplus). POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, not outside it. The rider's claim that the 380-second dwell is 'short of the 300 second minimum' is rejected: the free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds, 380 seconds exceeds it by 200 seconds, and the fee_schedule 300-second figure is retained only for pre-version-2 records and is never applied to a record that carries platform_policy. The driver's factual claims on arrival, dwell, rider presence and the corroboration of the arrival marker are accepted, but the POL-NS-07 payout claim and the 'NO_ACTION is a driver-side outcome' framing are rejected: POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limb (d) fails here, so no compensation is payable and the outcome is a refund to the rider, not NO_ACTION. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02723-01, weight 0.00, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact; its absence made POL-NS-06(i) unavailable, which changes nothing because no accumulation of separate intervals was needed. The referee discarded the driver-side advisory claim for citing that impaired artifact without naming its issue codes; it is not relied on. Integrity: nothing is impaired under POL-NS-08 - the 'arrived' event and the nearest GPS fix differ by 0 seconds, the maximum trace gap is 0 seconds, the 2-message chat log matches trip_record.chat_message_count of 2, and the SGD 4.50 cancellation line reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50 - so nothing is down-weighted and no POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged (no shared dispute history, no anti-farming pattern: no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against 114 completed trips in 30 days). Remedy: SGD 4.50 is refunded to the rider, and no driver compensation is paid. The monetary effect of SGD 4.50 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue; this ruling is provisional and either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: The driver's own cancellation reason code is DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which POL-NS-01(d) names as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. Limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT; DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is none of those, so limb (d) fails and the fee is not chargeable under the anchor clause.

The driver's in-geofence dwell was 380 seconds, which is short of the 300 second minimum dwell for a STANDARD zone class. The shortfall is 200 seconds against the required minimum, so even on the driver's best case the waiting period was not served and the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-06.

The rider was present and coordinating: her GPS track places her device within 15.5 m of the pickup pin for the whole window (67 qualifying fixes, all inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius), and she answered the driver's message at 12:00:59 saying she was at the lift lobby. The driver never replied and never placed an in-app call before cancelling at 12:06:23, so POL-NS-04 exonerates the rider and the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

The rider's own profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, so neither the POL-NS-09(d) abuse trigger nor the POL-NS-09(c) repeat-dispute trigger is engaged on the rider's side. There is no basis to treat this as a rider-abuse case.

The fare breakdown shows the full SGD 4.50 cancellation fee was charged to the rider and no refund has been issued (refund_issued_sgd 0.0, payment_status CHARGED). The contested amount is therefore live and a full refund of the cancellation-fee line is the correct remedy.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run: there is no advisory covering the pickup road and no basis to accumulate separate in-geofence intervals. The driver cannot rely on limb (i) to extend his dwell, and the 380 second run stands as the measured dwell.

The driver's own trace places him inside the STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous 380-second run, from 11:59:59 to 12:06:19, which is well past the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip. The dwell is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, exactly as POL-NS-01(c) requires, and the run is unbroken: 39 qualifying fixes, no gaps, 100% coverage.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 11:59:59, and the GPS trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at the same second, so the arrival marker is corroborated rather than false. There is no clock skew between the two artifacts and no motion at the marker: the driver's distinct speeds include 0.0 kph and the arrival run is stationary. POL-NS-05 therefore does not displace the waiting clock, and the dwell stands at 380 seconds.

The rider's own device was inside the 100 m rider-presence radius for the whole window: 67 qualifying fixes, all of them qualifying, mean distance 11.7 m from the pin, max 15.5 m, and a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph. The rider was stationary at the pickup point and did not board. That is the factual core of a no-show, and it is recorded on the rider's own track, not merely inferred from the driver's.

The chat log shows the driver asked 'cannot find you, where are you' at 12:00:29 and the rider answered 'at the lift lobby' at 12:00:59. The rider's answer names a sub-location but the driver had already been holding position inside the geofence for 30 seconds and continued to hold it for a further 5 minutes 20 seconds after that message before cancelling at 12:06:23. The driver did not abandon the pickup; he waited out the full free period and beyond.

The cancellation was recorded by the driver under reason code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE. I concede that this code is not one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, and that on the face of the clause limb (d) therefore fails. I do not stretch the record to call it RIDER_NO_SHOW. The consequence is that the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01, and the refund route must be found elsewhere in the category.

The driver's stationary fixes are inside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius, not outside it, so POL-NS-03 does not apply and the wrong-entrance route is closed. The rider's 'at the lift lobby' message does not identify a block, tower or bay that the driver failed to move to; it is a sub-location the driver could not act on because the rider never said which lift lobby of a Jurong West HDB block. POL-NS-03's fault allocation therefore does not strip the driver of compensation on these facts.

The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, and the driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 0 against 114 completed trips in 30 days. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires BOTH a count of 4 or more and a rate above 0.08; neither limb is met, so compensation is not withheld on that ground. I cite only the two fields POL-NS-07 and POL-NS-09(c) name, not the lifetime counters.

The fare ledger shows the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 charged to the rider, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the driver compensation computed at SGD 3.60, being 80 percent of the net fee under POL-NS-07. The fee line reconciles with the platform_policy figure of SGD 4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect and the money block is clean.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING: no advisory covers Blk 640 Jurong West St 61 in this window. I cite the absence itself. It means POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run to accumulate dwell across intervals, but it also means nothing in the record shows the driver was prevented from holding position, and the driver in fact held position for 380 seconds without needing any accumulation. The missing advisory is neutral to the driver's case and does not impair the arrival or dwell findings, which rest on the GPS trace alone.
